title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues sheet '2 bis'. That sheet's theorem concerns a cartesian square Y→X, Y→Y', X→X', Y'→X' in (Cat) with i', f (co)fibrations and a condition on fibres. Under that condition the canonical functor ∫(X ← Y → Y') → X' is a (co)fibration with aspherical fibres. The fibres have the form ∫(A = A → e) or ∫(A → e, A = A), which are cone-like and hence aspherical. So the functor lies in the basic localizer W, which means the strict pushout X' is W-equivalent to the Grothendieck-construction (homotopy) pushout. Corollary there: i ∈ W ⇒ i' ∈ W, and g ∈ W ⇒ f ∈ W.

This page applies that theorem to presheaves. Take a cocartesian square in Â with Y ↪ X a monomorphism. Then Y' ↪ X' is a monomorphism, since monos in a topos are stable under pushout. Apply i_A : Â → Cat, X ↦ A/X (category of elements). The resulting square A/Y → A/X, A/Y' → A/X' has three properties.
(i) It is cocartesian, because i_A commutes with small colimits; it is the left Kan extension of a ↦ A/a and has the right adjoint C ↦ Hom(A/(−), C).
(ii) It is cartesian, because i_A commutes with fibre products, and a pushout of a mono in a topos is also a pullback.
(iii) All arrows are discrete fibrations ('fibrantes'). The horizontal arrows are fibrant monomorphisms, i.e. sieves, which Grothendieck calls 'immersions ouvertes'.

So we are in the (dual, fibration) version of the theorem of p. 2 bis. Hence ∫(A/X ← A/Y → A/Y') → A/X' ∈ W, i.e. A/X' computes the homotopy pushout.

Corollary: if Y → X ∈ W_Â then Y' → X' ∈ W_Â (W_Â-trivial cofibrations are stable under cobase change). If Y → Y' ∈ W_Â then X → X' ∈ W_Â (pushout of any W_Â-equivalence along a mono is one, i.e. a left-properness type statement). Here W_Â = i_A^{-1}(W), and W is an arbitrary basic localizer on Cat.

Purpose: this is a key ingredient for showing that (Â, monos, W_Â) is a closed model structure, or at least that W_Â is stable under pushout along monos, for any basic localizer W. That is the question raised in Pursuing Stacks and later settled by Cisinski. The next page warns that the analogous statement fails for general pushouts in Cat, even along closed immersions, with a suspension/π1 counterexample. That is exactly why the passage through Â, where all maps are discrete fibrations, is needed.
errors: The fibre hypothesis transcribed on p. 2 bis ('f^{-1}(x') ou i'^{-1}(x') vide') does not literally hold in the present application. For x' in the image of Y', both fibres can be non-empty. What is actually needed, and holds here, is that each fibre of ∫(span) → A/X' is aspherical. If x' ∈ Y', the fibre is ∫(A = A → e) for a discrete set A, a cone, which is aspherical even when A = ∅. If x' ∉ Y', the f-fibre is a single point, since X'∖Y' ≅ X∖Y. The argument is correct but the stated hypothesis needs rephrasing.

The theorem of p. 2 bis is stated for cofibrations, while here the maps are fibrations. The marginal note 'remplacer avec fibrations' on p. 2 bis shows Grothendieck was aware that the dual version is what is used.

Gap: the asphericity of the fibres ∫(A = A → e) is only sketched on p. 2 bis (cone/retraction by deformation), and the passage from aspherical fibres of a fibration to membership in W uses the basic-localizer axioms (a Quillen-A-type property) implicitly. Both are standard, but neither is spelled out.

ideas.what: i_A : Â → Cat (category of elements) commutes with colimits and with fibre products, and sends monos to sieves/discrete fibrations
ideas.modern_name: Category of elements functor as left adjoint (nerve-realization adjunction i_A ⊣ i_A^*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); systematized by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski

ideas.what: The strict pushout of a span of discrete fibrations, one of them a sieve, is W-equivalent to its Grothendieck construction ∫ (homotopy pushout), for any basic localizer W
ideas.modern_name: Pushouts along sieves/Dwyer-type maps are homotopy pushouts; ∫ of a diagram as homotopy colimit (Thomason)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1980) for the Dwyer-map lemma and hocolim = Grothendieck construction; Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006) for arbitrary basic localizers
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; not found explicitly

ideas.what: For any basic localizer W and any small A, W_Â is stable under pushout along monomorphisms, and pushouts of W_Â-equivalences along monos are W_Â-equivalences
ideas.modern_name: Stability of trivial cofibrations under cobase change and left properness of the Cisinski model structure on Â attached to a basic localizer
ideas.usually_credited_to: D.-C. Cisinski, thesis (2002) and 'Les préfaisceaux comme modèles des types d'homotopie' (2006)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck raises the model-structure question in Pursuing Stacks; this proof via ∫ does not appear to be published

missed.claim: Grothendieck has a complete short argument that, for an arbitrary basic localizer W, W_Â-equivalences are stable under pushout along monomorphisms and that pushouts along monos preserve W_Â-equivalences. The argument runs: i_A preserves pushouts of monos, the resulting square in Cat is bicartesian with sieve and discrete-fibration edges, and its Grothendieck construction → strict pushout is a fibration with aspherical cone fibres. This is a core step of what is credited to Cisinski.
missed.quote: il est cocartésien (car i_A ... commute aux lim→) et cartésien (car i_A commute aux produits fibrés) et de plus les flèches sont fibrantes ... Corollaire Si (Y → X) ∈ W (resp. Y → Y' ∈ W) alors (Y' → X') ∈ W (resp. X → X' ∈ W)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck himself had the left-properness/cobase-change ingredient for general localizers, prefiguring Cisinski's theory. Combined with the next page's counterexample in Cat, it gives a clean conceptual explanation of why presheaves, not Cat, carry the model structure. It is of historical interest; mathematically it is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: The page gives a correct, self-contained proof of a key ingredient of the Cisinski model structure for an arbitrary basic localizer, via the Grothendieck construction and sieves. It is not routine, but the result is now well established and credited to Cisinski, and it is in the spirit of Pursuing Stacks. The value is mainly historical precedence rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The page number at the top is '3', continuing '2 bis'. The archive folio is 21.
'𝒦 [-mono-sous-cartésien-]' is most plausibly a struck-out qualifier, with the intended hypothesis simply 'Y ↪ X mono'.
'(tous indiqués)' is uncertain; it likely asserts that Y' → X' is mono by a standard topos fact (e.g. 'bien connu').
'donc ∫ A/X' vérifie ∫(…)' should be read as: the canonical functor ∫(A/X ← A/Y → A/Y') → A/X' is in W, i.e. A/X' is W-equivalent to ∫(…). The first '∫' before A/X' is probably a misreading.
'On est donc dans la situation dans les conditions énoncées' should probably read 'On est donc dans les conditions énoncées' (those of the Thm on p. 2 bis, fibration version).
The marginal 'Thm' at lower left marks this as a theorem.
